decisions.question: WSIP's shared evaluator averages per-slide validation losses in float64, while the original TransMIL sums the per-slide float32 logs and divides in float32. This makes val_loss (the early-stopping and checkpoint monitor) differ by up to one float32 ulp (measured 6e-8, at 1 of 9 epochs). Approve this as a recorded difference, or make the aggregation exact?
decisions.answered_by: Claude Opus 5.5 (PROVISIONAL, for Neal Parekh / Van Hovenga review)

decisions.question: Accept recorded difference `validation_loss_float64_mean`: The epoch validation loss (the early-stopping and checkpoint monitor) is the mean of the per-slide -log softmax[label]. The original stacks the per-slide float32 logs and sums and divides in float32 (utils/utils.py:cross_entropy_torch, logged by models/model_interface.py:validation_epoch_end); WSIP's shared evaluator averages the per-slide float32 losses in float64 (wsip/evaluation/evaluator.py:39). The per-slide losses are identical; only the final rounding of the mean differs. (evidence: ['upstream utils/utils.py:66-70', 'upstream models/model_interface.py:131', 'wsip/evaluation/evaluator.py:39'])
decisions.answered_by: Claude Opus 5.5 (PROVISIONAL, for Neal Parekh / Van Hovenga review)
